column1: # The conformance table for naming an agent identity.
# Naming an agent from a commit's author, committer or `Co-Authored-By` is
# written more than once, and the writings must not drift. This file is what
# every one of them is held to: the lists the recogniser is built from, and the
# people and agents it must tell apart. A row changed here fails whichever
# implementation disagrees, and an implementation changed without a row fails
# Format: `kind<TAB>value`, or `kind<TAB>value<TAB>value` where a row pairs two
# things. Blank lines and lines opening with `#` are ignored.
# The recogniser reads what only an agent carries, in this order. The words of a
# name are its letters and digits, lowercased, split at anything else.
#   marker     a bot marker, matched anywhere in the name or the mailbox;
#   mailbox    a mailbox an agent commits from, a glob over the whole mailbox
#              (`*` stands for any run of characters);
#   tag        a tag a tool writes into a name. A group in parentheses is read
#              only for these: a group holding exactly a tag makes the identity
#              an agent's (`Paul Gauthier (aider)`), and a group holding anything
#              else is left out of the name and says nothing about it (`Claude
#              3.5 Sonnet (new)` is read as `Claude 3.5 Sonnet`, `Jane Doe
#              (OpenAI)` is Jane Doe, and so is `Alex (Droid)` Alex). The set is
#   keyed      a name the project has said is an agent whatever its mailbox, and
#              an identity carrying it. The first value is what the project
#              sets, matched against the whole name, and the second is the
#              identity that then reads as an agent's. Without the project
#              saying so that identity is a person's, which is what the default
#   tool       a tool's own name, which makes an identity an agent's as the start
#              of a name: optionally behind `head` words, then the tool, then any
#              words at all (`Copilot Chat`, `Cursor Bugbot`). It has to be the
#              start, so a tool's name inside somebody's is none (`Smith
#   given      a tool whose name is also somebody's given name. As the start of a
#              name, behind `head` words if any, it is an agent when a
#              `companion` word is anywhere after it (`Claude Code Action`), when
#              nothing but versions follow it (`Claude 3.5`), or when nothing
#              follows it and either a `head` word stands in front (`Google
#              Gemini`) or the mailbox is the tool's: its local part is the tool's
#              word, the login after `NNN+` for a `users.noreply.github.com`
#              mailbox, or its domain is one of the tool's `vendor` domains,
#              matched whole. Any other word after it is a word of somebody's
#              name (`Claude Monet`, `Claude Max`). A version is a word opening
#              with a digit, or `v` and digits;
#   vendor     a given-name tool and a domain it commits from;
#   head       a vendor word allowed in front of a tool's name;
#   companion  a word that rides along with a tool: a model, a product, a surface.
# Below the lists come the verdicts: `person` rows are never an agent, `agent`
# rows always are, as an author, a committer and the value of a `Co-Authored-By`.
# --- the domains a given-name tool commits from ------------------------------
